unresolved.abstract: Nature controls reactivity through precisely organized secondary coordination spheres. Inspired by this principle, symmetry remodelling of a urea-functionalized iron porphyrin creates directional hydrogen-bonding interactions that enable unprecedented CO2 reduction in aprotic media and boost catalysis in the presence of a proton source. Optimal catalysis thus arises not only from intermediate stabilization but also from adaptive, directional non-covalent interactions. More in Research Article e1490828, Philipp Gotico, Marie Sircoglou, Zakaria Halime, and co-workers.
topics: Renewable Energy, Sustainability and the Environment

A Charge-Enhanced Hydrogen Bonding Strategy for Halogen Bond Activation in Catalysis
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Catalysis underpins modern chemical innovation, yet halogen-bond catalysts remain underdeveloped. Herein, we introduce a charged hydrogen bond-enhanced halogen bond (HBeXB) platform that intensifies σ-hole electrophilicity to unlock reactivity. Mechanistic, spectroscopic, and computational studies reveal a cooperative network of hydrogen bonding, halogen bonding, and nonclassical C–H interactions, delivering exceptional catalytic rates. The modular design of these scaffolds establishes a broadly applicable strategy for next generation organocatalysis.

unresolved.title: Synthesis of Diaryl α-Hydroxycarboxylic Acid Derivatives via Three-Component Reactions of o -Quinone Diimides with Alcohols and Diazo Compounds
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Highly regioselective three-component reactions of o-quinone diimides with alcohols and diazo compounds have been developed with a rhodium catalyst. This transformation is proposed to proceed through a Michael-type trapping of oxonium ylide intermediates with arylation reagents, giving access to a range of diaryl α-hydroxycarboxylic acid derivatives bearing an oxa-quaternary center in good yields. This reaction featured broad substrate scope, scale-up synthesis, and late-stage functionalization of the complex molecule.

unresolved.title: A method quantifying soil melanin to understand fungal impacts on soil carbon stability
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Fungal necromass, particularly dead microbial cells rich in melanin, is an important contributor to long-term soil carbon stabilization. Progress in understanding the role of soil melanin is limited by the lack of validated analytical methods. DNA-based approaches estimate only the genetic potential for melanin production and therefore provide indirect evidence of melanin occurrence. To directly assess soil melanin, we evaluated spectroscopic and spectrophotometric assays; however, both approaches proved insufficiently specific due to interference from chemically related compounds. Here, we introduce a liquid chromatography method that enables quantification of major fungal melanin types in soils. By enabling direct quantification of fungal melanin in soil, this framework allows longstanding hypotheses regarding melanized fungal necromass and soil carbon stabilization to be tested mechanistically. Here, we show with the proposed method that soil melanin concentrations are strongly correlated with total soil carbon, supporting a central role for fungal melanin in long-term soil carbon stabilization.

unresolved.title: An automated operon refactoring workflow for heterologous expression of non-ribosomal peptide biosynthetic gene clusters
unresolved.abstract: Microbial genomes encode numerous biosynthetic gene clusters, yet most remain experimentally uncharacterized, particularly large non-ribosomal peptide synthetase (NRPS) clusters that resist conventional cloning. Existing refactoring approaches are labor-intensive, depend on de novo DNA synthesis and are difficult to scale. Here we show that OSAR (One-Step Assembly and Refactoring)—an automated platform integrating algorithmic primer design with yeast homologous-recombination cloning—directly assembles and refactors NRPS clusters without custom DNA synthesis. We apply OSAR to 34 low- to medium-GC bacterial NRPS clusters (7–78 kb) and successfully assemble 31. Expression in Bacillus subtilis yields 29 peptides from 10 clusters. Several products arose from cryptic biosynthetic behaviors such as potential module skipping and premature release. OSAR provides a practical workflow for assembly and refactoring of NRPS clusters and may facilitate the translation of sequence information into natural products. Existing approaches for biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) discovery are labor-intensive, depend on de novo DNA synthesis and are difficult to scale. Here we show that an automated platform for one-step assembly and refactoring of BGCs facilitates facile novel product discovery.

unresolved.title: Asymmetric bloom lengthening drives high-latitude ocean chlorophyll accumulation imbalance
unresolved.abstract: Terrestrial ecosystems maintain a stable time-allocation budget between growth and senescence, but whether this applies to the ocean remains unclear. Using fused satellite LiDAR and ocean-color data (2007–2022), we show that marine phenology is variable and asymmetric. In high latitudes ( > 50°N), the bloom growth-to-decline ratio (RGD) is declining by ~5.3% per decade. While the chlorophyll-increase phase has lengthened by 2.3–5.5 days, the post-peak chlorophyll-decline phase has extended disproportionately by 5.7–6.2 days. Environmental sensitivity analyses reveal distinct hemispheric patterns in the statistical associations between phenological variability and multiple co-varying physical and biogeochemical factors, consistent with contrasting nutrient regimes between the Northern and Southern high-latitude oceans. We further show that these shifts are associated with spatially heterogeneous changes in marine chlorophyll accumulation patterns. Our results identify bloom asymmetry as an important dimension of marine phenological change, providing an observational baseline for evaluating future links between chlorophyll phenology, ecosystem timing, and polar biogeochemical processes under climate change. This study shows that unequal changes in bloom duration between hemispheres contribute to contrasting high-latitude ocean chlorophyll trends, linking asymmetric phytoplankton

unresolved.title: In situ reduction-driven formation of sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures
unresolved.abstract: Sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures provide a platform for modulating electronic structure and interfacial reactivity through strong atom-level coupling, with potential applications in energy conversion. However, their precise construction remains challenging. Here we show a strategy for constructing sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures through confined spinodal decomposition and ligand-mediated in situ reduction. Oleylamine ligands adsorbed on NiMoO4 sub-nanowires act as mild reductants, selectively reducing Ni2+ to spatially confined metallic Ni domains and forming coherent Ni/NiMoO4 heterointerfaces. Experimental and theoretical analyses suggest that the Ni/NiMoO4 interfaces modify the local electronic structure and facilitate the adsorption and activation of hydrogen evolution intermediates. The resulting catalyst requires an overpotential of 14.4 ± 2.9 mV to reach 10 mA cm−2 in 1 M KOH and delivers 2 A cm−2 at 1.62 V in an anion-exchange membrane electrolyzer at 80 oC, with stable operation over 2200 h at 25 °C. These findings provide insights into the construction and interfacial regulation of sub-nanometer heterostructures through in situ reduction. Sub-nanometer heterostructures offer opportunities to tune interfacial reactivity, but their precise construction remains challenging. unresolved.title: Intensification of near-inertial currents in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades
unresolved.abstract: Near-inertial currents (NICs) play a key role in surface material redistribution and ocean mixing, yet their long-term variability remains poorly known. Using in situ current measurements from surface drifters, we provide observational evidence for a pronounced intensification of surface NICs in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades (2003–2022). Basin–mean NIC strength increases at a rate of 3.8 ± 1.7% per decade, with a spatial pattern characterized by strengthening in the South Atlantic and the high-latitude North Atlantic, and weakening in the low-latitude North Atlantic. We further show that these trends in Atlantic NICs are primarily driven by changes in near-inertial wind forcing, particularly those associated with mesoscale weather systems, while variations in mixed-layer depth playing a minor role. This observed intensification of Atlantic NICs may have important implications for ocean transport and mixing, and needs to be properly represented in the current generation of climate models. Ocean drifter observations reveal that Atlantic near-inertial currents intensified by almost 4% per decade during 2003–2022. This intensification is primarily driven by changes in wind forcing associated with mesoscale weather systems.

unresolved.title: Curvature-Induced Electric-Field Effects Govern Controllable N2 Electrocatalysis on Single-Atom Catalysts
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Electric field-enhanced electrocatalysis represents an innovative strategy for improving the efficiency of electrochemical transformations. However, quantitative evaluation of microscopic electric-field effects under operando conditions remains challenging, limiting a rigorous, predictive understanding of field-mediated reaction regulation. Here, by integrating rigorous numerical methods, constant-potential microkinetic simulations, and machine learning models, we establish electric-field intensity as a quantitative descriptor that directly correlates local fields with catalytic performance. Using curvature-engineered M–N–C single-atom catalysts as a model platform, we demonstrate that curvature-induced electric fields modulate electron occupation at active sites and shift the potential of zero charge in a controllable manner. This field-driven electronic perturbation selectively tunes adsorbate binding energetics, thereby dictating limiting potentials, steering reaction pathways, and governing the thermodynamics and kinetics of interfacial proton-coupled electron transfer in nitrogen electroreduction. Notably, we uncover an inverted volcano–type dependence of catalytic activity on curvature, wherein optimal activity is achieved within a moderate field-strength window. This nonmonotonic trend underscores the necessity of balanced curvature regulation, rather than simpl
topics: Renewable Energy, Sustainability and the Environment

unresolved.title: Diffusion-Selective Modulation Strategy for Enhanced Propane Dehydrogenation via Mixing Inert CHA Zeolite
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Achieving a high propane conversion in propane dehydrogenation to propylene (PDH) carries tremendous scientific and economic value, particularly if achievable with established industrial units. Here we propose a diffusion-selective modulation strategy driven by large-scale machine-learning computation, where the key to success lies in finding auxiliary materials to drive the PDH reaction forward by enlarging the diffusion-rate difference between H2 and C3 species. This strategy is demonstrated theoretically via high-throughput computation and then validated experimentally through the introduction of inert siliceous CHA zeolites as a diffusion-selective modulator within the catalyst bed. By simply physically mixing CHA with various PDH catalysts, we show that the single-pass propane conversion can increase by 1–5% from industrial space velocities (10 h–1) to significantly higher throughputs (256 h–1), consistently improving performance across multiple reported catalysts without compromising stability. This “plug-and-play” methodology can be directly implemented in existing industrial PDH units without altering either the catalyst formulation or the reactor configuration, providing a readily implementable and scalable route for upgrading current PDH infrastructure.

unresolved.abstract: "My long-term goal is the development of nucleic acid-based molecular systems that allow us to see and interact with biological systems… The most exciting thing about my research is seeing the beauty and complexity of the molecular composition of life…" Find out more about Fan Hong in his Introducing… Profile.

unresolved.title: A dual-attribution framework reveals how foreign investment and trade redistribute cobalt availability
unresolved.abstract: Global resource allocation is increasingly shaped by foreign direct investment (FDI) and international trade, yet their combined effects on distribution of critical mineral availability across countries remain poorly quantified. Here, we develop a dual-attribution framework covering 193 countries and 36 territories that attributes primary cobalt availability according to corporate ownership and secondary availability according to international trade. We compare these estimates with a combined baseline scenario using geographic-production and pre-trade perspectives to assess how ownership and trade reshape country-level cobalt availability. Relative to this baseline, total cobalt availability is higher in 63.6% of countries, while 72.7% show a positive composite change when primary and secondary availability are equally weighted. Although these mechanisms do not alter the global total amount of cobalt available, they reduce its concentration across countries. Our findings highlight how FDI and trade reshape cobalt distribution and support resource-governance policies that account for both host and exporting countries. This study shows how foreign investment and international trade reshape global cobalt availability. A dual-attribution framework reveals higher attributed availability in most countries while reducing country-level concentration.

unresolved.title: A self-limiting mechanotransduction feedback loop ensures robust organ formation
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Organ morphogenesis uses mechanotransduction feedback loops to convert forces into gene expression changes that regulate cell mechanics. How these loops integrate with developmental programs to ensure robust outcomes remains unclear. We show Yap mechanotransduction establishes a self-limiting positive feedback loop for semicircular canal formation in zebrafish. Canal development proceeds through bud initiation, extension, and fusion within the otic epithelium. Local swelling of hyaluronan-rich extracellular matrix (ECM) in the bud activates Yap in a spatial pattern. Yap induces its target ccn1l1 , promoting further ECM expansion to sustain bud extension. This feedback loop confers developmental robustness: graded knockdown of ccn1l1 reduces extension rate, yet canal formation persists and fails only with strong disruption. Critically, the loop contains its own termination mechanism. During bud fusion, PKA-CREB signaling, activated by an adhesion GPCR, gpr126, suppresses ccn1l1 , ending the loop. These findings reveal how mechanotransduction loops with built-in termination provide developmental control by integrating mechanical forces, transcriptional responses, and morphogenetic outcomes.

unresolved.title: Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis is concomitant with reduced metacognitive efficiency and sensitivity across multiple cohorts and modalities
unresolved.abstract: The corpus callosum is the largest commissure in the mammalian brain and has been implicated in supporting cognitive processes required for adapting to complex environments. Individuals born with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis, characterized by malformations of the corpus callosum, commonly exhibit deficits in social navigation, abstract problem-solving, decision-making, and self-awareness. Metacognition is a key cognitive process that supports these functions; however, it has yet to be tested comprehensively in individuals with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis. Over three experiments, and three Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis cohorts, we examine perceptual accuracy, confidence judgments, and metacognitive efficiency in individuals with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis using two variants of a Random Dot Kinematogram task within lab, online, and virtual reality conditions. We find that individuals with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis typically display normal perceptual accuracy but fail to adjust their confidence judgments in line with task difficulty. Computational modeling reveal that this difference is characterized by lower metacognitive efficiency concomitant with lower metacognitive sensitivity. Together, these results provide evidence that the corpus callosum is consistently associated with reduced metacognitive efficiency. unresolved.title: Giant step-boundary-triggered nonlocal modulation of magnetization reversal in multi-stepped van der Waals ferromagnet Fe3GaTe2
unresolved.abstract: Control of magnetization reversal is crucial for spintronic memory and logic devices. Previous studies on two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) magnets have largely treated magnetic regions in isolation, leaving the roles of step boundaries comparatively unexplored. Here, we investigate step-boundary-triggered nonlocal modulation of magnetization reversal in multi-stepped Fe3GaTe2 using Kerr microscopy, Lorentz transmission electron microscopy, and micromagnetic simulations. Our results indicate that step boundaries can serve as preferential sites for premature nucleation, giving rise to two distinct regimes. In Type I, reversal initiated in a thicker region propagates rapidly across the step boundary, reducing the coercivity of an adjacent thinner region by up to 59.3%. In Type II, stripe domains originating from the thicker region progressively enter the thinner region, shifting its critical switching field polarity and transforming its hysteresis loop from square to slanted, accompanied by a transition in the dominant reversal mode from rapid domain-wall motion to stripe domain growth. Similar behavior in Fe3GeTe2 suggests that step-boundary-mediated modulation may occur more broadly in layered van der Waals ferromagnets. Our findings highlight step engineering as a potential non-invasive strategy for designing efficient and thermally stable vdW spintronic devices. Bounda

unresolved.title: Intrinsically flexible inorganic piezoelectric subnanowire enables wireless wearable bioelectronics for non-invasive multimodal human-machine interfacing
unresolved.abstract: Piezoelectric electronic skin (PE-skin) offers a significant advantage in detecting minute forces, making it highly promising for human-computer interaction in health management and medical rehabilitation. However, PE-skin often faces challenges in real-time, wireless transmission of sensing data, which can compromise both data accuracy and user comfort. Here, we report the synthesis of an inorganic piezoelectric polyoxometalate-based subnanowire, ZnBiPMo12, which possesses intrinsic flexibility and chirality, a piezoelectric coefficient of 24.9 pC/N, and notable ferroelectricity. Leveraging its piezoelectric response, ZnBiPMo12-based PE-skin (1) demonstrates high elasticity and sensitivity to tiny pressures in the range of 0.045-0.319 N. Building on this, a wireless, wearable bioelectronic (WBE) device (1A) is fabricated through multi-level assembly, enabling non-invasive, multimodal monitoring of human physiological signals, including subtle muscle contractions, blinking, breathing, and all-day heart rate. By integrating a machine learning system, a 1-based facial-computer interface (1B) can accurately recognize nine emotional expressions and twelve spoken words. This work not only introduces a typical inorganic piezoelectric material with intrinsic flexibility but also demonstrates scalable manufacturing from subnanomaterials to wireless WBEs, paving the way for non-invasive
topics: Advanced Sensor and Energy Harvesting Materials

unresolved.title: Long-term nitrous acid evolution modulates ozone and secondary aerosol variations in global megacities
unresolved.abstract: Nitrous acid (HONO) is a crucial urban source of HOx radicals, promoting surface ozone (O3) and secondary fine particle (PM2.5) formation, yet its long-term evolution and air-quality impacts remain poorly constrained. Here, using a deep neural network established on worldwide field campaigns, we reconstruct global surface HONO distributions. Typical megacities exhibited contrasting trends in 2005–2021, marked by a sharp decline in Beijing (−47.4% in 2013–2021), an increase in Delhi (+10.0% in 2005–2018), and slight decreases in London, New York and Los Angeles. These HONO changes are identified as major driver of O3 and particulate nitrate variations, outweighing contributions of conventional NOx and volatile organic compounds abatement in Beijing and Delhi, while showing comparable impacts in the remaining cities. A fused data-driven framework further uncovers regime-dependent HONO reduction strategies, prioritizing NOx control in summer and co-reduction of NOx, PM2.5 and direct combustion emissions in winter, to accelerate O3 and PM2.5 joint mitigation. Deep learning reveals a sharp decline of HONO in China, modest drops in EU and US but an increase in India. HONO changes drive O3 and PM2.5 variations, outweighing traditional NOx and VOC control, calling for HONO-targeted air quality management.

unresolved.title: PRPF19 drives hepatic stellate cell activation and liver fibrosis via PKM2-mediated glycolytic reprogramming
unresolved.abstract: Activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) is a pivotal event driving fibrogenic remodeling of the injured liver. However, the upstream regulators that integrate post-translational signaling with metabolic reprogramming during HSC activation remain poorly defined. Here, we identify pre-mRNA processing factor 19 (PRPF19) as a ubiquitination-linked metabolic regulator that promotes HSC activation. PRPF19 expression was elevated in human and murine fibrotic livers, enriched in activated HSCs, and positively correlated with fibrosis severity. Conditional deletion of Prpf19 in HSCs (Prpf19flox/flox;Lrat-CreERT2), but not in hepatocytes (Prpf19flox/flox;Alb-CreERT2), attenuated HSC activation and liver fibrosis in vivo. Integrated transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses indicated that PRPF19 sustains glycolytic flux and transcriptional programs associated with HSC activation. Mechanistically, PRPF19 promoted K63-linked ubiquitination of pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2), facilitating its nuclear translocation and hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α)-dependent transcription of glycolytic and fibrogenic genes. These findings support a role for the PRPF19-PKM2 pathway in metabolic regulation during HSC activation and liver fibrosis. unresolved.title: Quantum-sensing-based super-resolution live cell microenvironment imaging
unresolved.abstract: Direct monitoring the multifaceted intracellular microenvironment is fundamental for deciphering localized cellular behavior and function. However, performing nanoscale spatiotemporal sensing of the dynamic physiochemical environment within a live cell has remained challenging, mainly limited by the lack of robust, biocompatible method which satisfies the requirements for spatiotemporal resolution, sensitivity, multi-physical sensing capability and long-term viability. Here we present a super-resolution-based quantum biosensing approach, namely Super-resolution Multi-physical field Imaging with Deconvolution, implemented in our custom-built setup which integrates nitrogen vacancy center-based quantum sensing with structured illumination microscopy. This enables quantitative, super-resolved, and long-term tracking of intracellular physical fields, featuring spatial resolution of 136 nm, temporal resolution of 150 ms, and field of view of 180×180 μm2. We further perform super-resolution multimodal imaging in a live cell, revealing the spatially heterogeneous reactive oxygen species dynamics under external stimulation. Our work enables the dynamic assessment of localized physiochemical dynamics under super-resolution quantum biosensing. This work presents a super-resolution quantum biosensing approach by integrating nitrogen vacancy (NV) center-based quantum nanodiamond sensors wi

unresolved.title: Transposable element-mediated structural variations shape gene expression and agronomic trait diversity in Brassica napus
unresolved.abstract: Brassica napus is a globally important allotetraploid oilseed crop with a complex genome and extensive structural diversity that remains incompletely characterized. Here, we present gap-free reference genome assemblies for Zhongshuang 11 (ZS11) and Westar, and assemble six additional accessions. We harmonize gene annotations across 22 genomes and develop BnaScope (https://rgmi.hzau.edu.cn/bnascope), a gene-centric functional genomics platform. Gene-based and graph-based pan-genomes identify 123,107 non-redundant gene clusters and 188,218 structural variants, including 112,417 transposable element-mediated structural variants (TEMSVs). TEMSVs show asymmetric distributions between An and Cn subgenomes and are associated with increased homoeolog expression imbalance, particularly for CDS-TEMSVs. SV-based genome-wide association analyses identify candidate genes underlying seed quality traits, and functional analyses demonstrate that BnaPYRDs negatively regulate seed glucosinolate content. These findings establish structural variation as an important contributor to homoeolog regulation and seed-quality variation in B. napus. This study develops a comprehensive pan-genome resource for Brassica napus and reveals how structural variations shape gene regulation and seed quality traits. The findings provide insights into genome diversity and crop improvement.
topics: Genetic Mapping and Diversity in Plants and Animals

unresolved.title: A cross-layer 2D photodetection framework for standardized readout and signal fusion
unresolved.abstract: Beyond improving device responsivity, a central challenge in photodetectors based on two-dimensional (2D) materials is to resolve the information-interface mismatch and delayed system translation caused by trap-governed persistent photoconductivity (PPC). Here we present a cross-layer engineering route oriented towards practical implementation that integrates defect-mechanism analysis, non-stationary signal definition, dynamic distortion compensation and readout-interface engineering, thereby establishing a conversion pathway from physical response to system output in 2D MoS2, WSe2 and PtSe2 photodetectors. In this context, drift, hysteresis and fatigue accumulation in time-varying photoresponses are no longer treated merely as non-ideal perturbations, but are reformulated as state-dependent information that can be defined, compensated and interfaced. Through interface restructuring and stable readout, nW-level state-dependent photocurrents are systematically mapped onto a mixed-signal readout interface. We further extend this strategy to array-level unified output and multisensor fusion, with its frequency-guided representation evaluated in a machine-vision task. Our results show that the history-dependent nonlinear response governed by PPC is not simply a local device non-ideality, but a state-encoded signal linking defect dynamics, readout pathways and system-level tasks. unresolved.title: Antisense oligonucleotides targeting transcription termination windows disrupt mRNA 3’ end processing and decrease gene expression
unresolved.abstract: ABSTRACT Antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) are short, synthetic nucleic acids that bind to complementary RNA sequences and alter gene expression, making them versatile therapeutic agents. Here, we identify transcription termination windows of protein-coding genes as previously unrecognized targets for ASOs. We show that ASOs can act on nascent RNA synthesised downstream of the annotated genes, leading to a pronounced decrease in the corresponding mRNA levels. These downstream-of-gene ASOs (DG-ASOs) induce RNase H1-dependent cleavage, impairing mRNA 3’ end processing, directing the unprocessed mRNAs for exosome-dependent degradation and creating early entry points in the nascent RNA for the XRN2 exonuclease termination factor. Altogether, we show that termination windows are genuine ASO targets which can be exploited to suppress gene expression. Importantly, we also reveal an underappreciated source of off-target effects which may arise from ASOs binding downstream of genes. Our findings indicate the necessity to expand ASO design and off-target assessment guidelines to include termination window sequences, thereby improving therapeutic efficacy and safety.

unresolved.title: ATM promotes nucleolytic processing of reversed replication forks during DNA interstrand cross-link repair
unresolved.abstract: During replication-coupled DNA interstrand cross-link (ICL) repair, fork reversal is thought to enable the Fanconi anemia (FA) pathway to resolve the ICL through nucleolytic incisions. The resulting regressed arm of the reversed fork undergoes extensive nucleolytic resection that may facilitate completion of replication. Despite the importance of these remodeling events, their regulation remains poorly understood. Here, we use cell-free Xenopus egg extracts and human cells to investigate reversed fork processing during ICL repair by the FA pathway. We find that the ataxia-telangiectasia mutated (ATM) kinase is activated concomitantly with fork reversal and promotes resection of reversed fork intermediates. ATM enhances chromatin recruitment of DNA2, which acts alongside EXO1 to resect reversed forks formed during ICL repair. Moreover, inhibition of protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A) leads to ATM hyperactivation, accelerated reversed fork processing, and accumulation of aberrant end-joining products, implying that PP2A restrains ATM signaling to limit reversed fork resection. Taken together, this work identifies reversed forks as substrates for ATM activation and reveals a phospho-regulatory circuit that controls reversed fork processing. unresolved.title: Bias-reconfigurable barrier photodetectors for integrated broadband sensing and neuromorphic vision
unresolved.abstract: Intelligent vision systems demand photodetectors with reconfigurable response to support diverse modalities like high-speed sensing and neuromorphic processing. Here we show a bias-reconfigurable barrier photodetector that enables continuous modulation of response time across 7 orders of magnitude, from 614 ns to 8.28 s. This wide-range tunability is achieved by electrically modulating the interfacial barrier height, which switches the dominant carrier transport mechanism from direct tunneling to barrier-limited thermal excitation and trap-assisted processes. Under low bias, the device functions as a high-speed photodetector, whereas elevated biases extend the response to synaptic timescales, enabling in-sensor neuromorphic computing as a physical reservoir. Notably, the device exhibits a broadband photoresponse from visible to mid-infrared. High accuracy was achieved in complex recognition tasks, such as classifying vehicle acceleration or deceleration. This integration of fast photodetection and neuromorphic computation establishes hardware-efficient paradigms for integrated machine vision, adaptive multispectral sensing, and energy-efficient edge intelligence. Intelligent vision systems require diverse functionalities, ranging from high-speed sensing to neuromorphic processing. unresolved.title: CROSS: A cross-species chromosome substitution platform for dissecting chromosome architecture and activity
unresolved.abstract: The functional integrity of a mammalian chromosome depends on its long-term co-evolution with species-specific nuclear environment. How chromosomes co-adapt with their native environment to define 3D architecture and transcription remains unclear, largely due to a lack of experimental models that dissect this co-evolution. Here, we report cross-species chromosome substitution (CROSS), a method enabling stable, scarless replacement of host chromosomes with divergent orthologs. We integrate microcell-mediated chromosome transfer with CRISPR/Cas9 to import the intact 152-Mb rat X chromosome into male mouse embryonic stem cells, and subsequently replace the mouse X chromosome, maintaining its stability and integrity. Rat-specific LINE1 and RatSatRep2 repeats recruit mouse SETDB1 inefficiently, causing local H3K9me3 loss. This triggers 3D remodeling, characterized by de novo topologically associating domain (TAD) boundaries that aberrantly activate adjacent genes, including Rhox5, impairing differentiation. We provide a platform for dissecting sequence and epigenome cooperation in chromosome regulation, and evaluating fidelity of large-scale heterologous DNA. Chromosome function depends on coevolution with nuclear environment, but how is unclear. Here, authors use CROSS to stably and scarlessly replace mouse chrX with rat chrX. Rat repeats poorly recruit SETDB1, causing H3K9me3 loss

unresolved.title: De novo design of miniprotein inhibitors of bacterial adhesins
unresolved.abstract: The rise of multidrug-resistant bacterial infections necessitates the discovery of novel antimicrobial strategies. Here, we show that protein design provides a generalizable means of generating new antimicrobials by neutralizing the function of bacterial adhesins, which are virulence factors critical in host-pathogen interactions. We de novo designed high-affinity miniprotein binders to FimH and Abp chaperone usher pili adhesins from uropathogenic Escherichia coli and Acinetobacter baumannii, respectively, which are implicated in mediating both uncomplicated and catheter-associated urinary tract infections (UTI) responsible for significant morbidity worldwide. The designed antagonists have high specificity and stability, disrupt bacterial recognition of host receptors, block biofilm formation, and are effective in treating and preventing murine models of uncomplicated and catheter-associated UTIs in vivo. Here, the authors show that protein design is a generalizable strategy to generate new antimicrobials by neutralizing the function of bacterial adhesins to combat two causative agents of urinary tract infections, E. coli and A. baumannii.

unresolved.title: Environmentally Relevant Concentrations of Nanomaterials Drive Photochemical Production of Reactive Species and Pollutant Degradation in Surface Waters
unresolved.abstract: Reactive intermediates in surface waters are widely attributed to dissolved organic matter (DOM). Natural, incidental, or engineered nanomaterials simultaneously occur at parts per billion and can function as photocatalysts, yet the photochemical role of nanomaterials at environmentally relevant concentrations remains overlooked in surface water photochemistry. Here, we quantify reactive intermediates from TiO2 nanomaterials (1–100 μg L−1) and DOM (1–5 mgC L−1) under 222, 265, and 365 nm. Despite lower concentrations relative to DOM, TiO2 produces hydroxyl radical (HO•) rates 10× to 100× higher per unit mass, resulting in comparable HO• formation. DOM plus nanomaterial mixtures shows synergistic behavior, with HO• formation 16-21% above additive predictions. DOM has limited impact in the degradation of 6PPD-quinone whereas nanomaterials enhanced its degradation due to elevated [HO•]ss. These results demonstrate nanomaterials can contribute to or exceed DOM in HO• driven micropollutant degradation in surface waters or engineered ultraviolet-light water treatment systems. Environmentally relevant nanomaterial concentrations can rival dissolved organic matter in driving pollutant transformation under sunlight or UV-based water treatment.

unresolved.title: Fast-charging and durable all-solid-state lithium-sulfur batteries enabled by pre-embedded solid-solid redox mediator
unresolved.abstract: All-solid-state lithium-sulfur batteries promise high specific energy and low cost. However, they are challenged by poor rate capability and cycling stability owing to the slow solid-solid sulfur redox reactions. Here, we present fast-charging and durable all-solid-state lithium-sulfur batteries enabled by a pre-embedded solid-solid redox mediator using an amorphous sulfur/iodine nano-eutectic positive electrode. The iodine, intimately homogenized with sulfur owing to carbon mesopore encapsulation, undergoes rapid I2/I− redox reaction, mediating solid-solid sulfur reactions by promoting electron transfer across the boundaries. The iodine within the carbon and on its surface reacts in situ with the sulfide catholyte to form a globally distributed I2/I− nano-network throughout the positive electrode, thereby enabling fast charging. The cell exhibits a specific capacity of 851.9 mA h g−1S/I when charged at 10 C, and 474.7 mA h g−1S/I at a charging rate of 24 C (1 C is defined as 945 mA g−1S/I). The high reversibility of the redox-mediated reaction enables durable cycling for 9,000 cycles over 9 months at 2 C and 2,800 cycles over 17 months at 0.5 C. This strategy represents a perspective for developing solid-state conversion electrodes that are plagued by sluggish reactions. unresolved.title: Freezing-induced solid-liquid microphase separation for self-assembly of functional nucleic acid nanoparticles
unresolved.abstract: In nature, nuclear DNA complexed with histone form highly condensed chromatin via loop extrusion and microphase separation, yielding physically constrained solid-like structures. Inspired by this natural compaction, here we demonstrate that freezing-induced crystallization pressure and freeze-concentration effects trigger solid-liquid microphase separation for efficient DNA compression. Freezing compress various nucleic acids (single stranded DNA, molecular beacons, siRNA, plasmid DNA) into high-density states that self-assemble into nanoparticles (DNA-NPs, MB-NPs, siBcl-2-NPs, siPLK1-NPs, pEGFP-NPs). Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that ice crystal growth increases solute concentration, enhancing DNA intermolecular interactions to form supramolecular chains. Stress at advancing ice-liquid interfaces further orders and compacts these supramolecular chains into nanoparticles. In breast cancer cells, MB-NPs detect miRNA-21; siBcl-2-NPs downregulate Bcl-2 protein; siPLK1-NPs exhibited antitumor effects; and pEGFP-NPs mediate green fluorescent protein (GFP) expression. This freeze-induced self-assembly strategy replaces chemical synthesis with physical constraints, establishing a versatile platform for facile production of nucleic acid nanoparticles. Efficent delivery of various nucleic acids in vitro and in vivo remains challenging. Here, the authors use freezing-induced con

unresolved.title: Genome architecture drives antifungal resistance in Candida auris
unresolved.abstract: Antifungal resistance often results from mutations in drug target genes. However, Narayanan et al. show that segmental duplication and supernumerary chromosomes also contribute to resistance in the emerging fungal pathogen Candida auris. The work expands the genetic basis of antifungal resistance and redefines the mutation-centric paradigm.

unresolved.title: Genotype-phenotype single-cell transcriptomics for massive parallel assessment of genetic variants
unresolved.abstract: Predicting the pathogenic effect of rare genetic variants is significantly hampered by the limited cohort of diagnosed patients and the difficulty in functionally evaluating the effect of existing and novel variants. To address this issue, we leveraged a protein Multiplexed Assay of Variants Effect (MAVE) to functionally assess the effect of ~ 2200 missense variants of the TP63 gene, some of which cause autosomal dominant developmental disorders. The activity of each variant was measured using an optimized fibroblast-to-keratinocyte conversion protocol, and a subset of mutants was validated through multiple orthogonal biochemical and genomics functional assays to assess consistency and robustness. To systematically expand MAVEs beyond predefined assay, we here introduce SCRAMseq (Single Cell RNAseq Associated with MAVEs by sequencing). This generalizable platform leverages full-length scRNAseq for high-throughput, single-cell genotype-to-phenotype mapping. We validate SCRAMseq across different experimental and genetic contexts to demonstrate its reproducibility and accuracy. SCRAMseq provides a robust and versatile workflow poised to accelerate the discovery and dissection of gene variant effects on any potential disease-driving pathway, thereby significantly broadening MAVEs applicability to virtually any possible disease-driving gene. This work introduces SCRAMseq, a generali

unresolved.title: High-resolution spatial transcriptomics reveals fibroblast and neuroimmune microenvironments in endometriosis lesions
unresolved.abstract: Endometriosis is a chronic, systemic, inflammatory disease characterized by the presence of endometrium-like tissue growing outside of the uterus. Affecting one in ten individuals assigned female at birth, it causes chronic pain and inflammation that significantly impairs quality of life. Yet the mechanisms that drive pain and disease progression remain poorly defined. This study establishes the precise spatial transcriptomic cartography of human ovarian and peritoneal lesions, two of the most commonly found lesions. We identify shared spatial features across lesion types, including immune cell infiltration, fibroblast compartments surrounding epithelial glands, and distinct distributions of neuronal and macrophage subsets. We precisely defined sensory neuronal subtypes and mapped their spatial location relative to immune cells. We further validate the epithelial-neuronal interactome, using an in vitro 3D model of peripheral sensory brain organoids co-cultured with human endometriosis epithelial and fibroblast cells. By mapping spatial cellular interactions and conserved features across lesion types linked to pain, our study advances understanding of endometriosis pathophysiology and informs targeted therapeutic development. Haney et al. map human endometriosis lesions and reveal shared cellular organization across endometriosis lesion types, identifying fibroblast compartments

unresolved.title: Lipid-organized tetramerization of PLPP1 defines the molecular basis of spatial lipid phosphate signaling
unresolved.abstract: Bioactive lipid phosphates, such as lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) and sphingosine-1-phosphate, are potent membrane-embedded signals that regulate fundamental processes in development, immunity, and cancer. The termination of these signals is mediated by phospholipid phosphatases (PLPPs), yet the molecular principles governing their function at the membrane interface have remained poorly understood. Here we report high-resolution cryo-electron microscopy structures of human PLPP1 in apo (1.87 Å) and product-bound (2.21 Å) states. The structures reveal a highly ordered, C4-symmetric homotetramer with ordered lipid densities—including densities assigned to phosphatidylcholine, phosphatidic acid, and phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate—at inter-subunit interfaces. Structure-guided mutagenesis shows that residues surrounding these interfacial lipid densities affect enzymatic activity, whereas oligomerization analysis indicates that activity loss does not simply correlate with tetramer disruption. The product-bound structure defines the catalytic pocket and a membrane-facing tunnel that suggests a possible route for LPA access, while electrophysiological recordings detected no PLPP1-associated ion conductance under the conditions tested. Together, these findings provide a structural framework for PLPP1 tetramer assembly, lipid phosphate hydrolysis, and product recognition. Lipid phos
topics: Protein Kinase Regulation and GTPase Signaling

unresolved.title: MACF1 condensates serve as molecular rheostats translating mechanical stress into bone adaptation
unresolved.abstract: Bone dynamically maintains homeostasis through mechanotransduction, a process essential for skeletal integrity and frequently disrupted in disease. Yet how bone cells decode mechanical cues into adaptive responses remains poorly understood. Here, we identify MACF1, a cytoskeletal crosslinker and core component of stress granules (SGs), as a mechanosensitive scaffold that undergoes phase separation via its intrinsically disordered region 2 (IDR2). In response to distinct mechanical cues, IDR2-driven condensation promotes the recruitment of PIEZO1, paxillin (PXN), and β-catenin (CTNNB1) into SGs, buffering these signaling molecules from ubiquitination-dependent degradation and sustaining osteogenic fidelity. Moreover, we identify an arginine-mutated IDR2 variant that separates protein interactions from condensate formation, revealing IDR2-driven phase separation as a requirement for MACF1-mediated SG assembly and mechanosensitive protein recruitment. Functionally, bone-targeted delivery of MACF1-IDR2 alleviates mechanical unloading-induced bone loss in male mice. These findings reveal a liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS)-mediated mechanism linking mechanical force sensing and transduction to bone adaptation. Together, these findings support a model in which MACF1 condensates act as molecular rheostats that coordinate mechano-responsive cargo sorting under stress and contribute

unresolved.title: Multi-omics profiling uncovers diagnostic biomarker panel, progression-associated subtypes, and prognostic signature in pediatric mitochondrial disease
unresolved.abstract: Pediatric mitochondrial disease (PMD) is challenging due to its genetic heterogeneity, diagnostic difficulty, and unpredictable trajectories. Current biomarkers lack sensitivity to diagnose PMD or predict its severe course. Here, we show a multi-omics framework with longitudinal monitoring to resolve these challenges. We identify metabolic and transcriptomic dysregulation in PMD, deriving a robust 7-feature multi-omics diagnostic panel (6 metabolites, 1 transcript). In an independent validation cohort, this panel achieved superior diagnostic accuracy (AUC = 0.96) compared to conventional biomarkers. Beyond diagnosis, we addressed the need for patient stratification. Unsupervised proteomic clustering revealed two subtypes (Cluster I and II) that diverged over time; Cluster II patients had downregulation of cytoskeletal and immune pathways and worse clinical outcomes at 12 months. We leveraged these insights to develop a 12-transcript prognostic signature that predicts clinical prognostication with high accuracy (AUC = 0.85). This study establishes a molecular framework for PMD, offering validated tools for precision diagnosis and prognostic stratification. Pediatric mitochondrial disease lacks reliable biomarkers. Here, the authors show that a multi-omics study identified a 7-feature diagnostic panel (AUC = 0.96), revealed two proteomic subtypes with differing outcomes, and deve

unresolved.title: Non-sewered sanitation systems reshape microplastics into chemically complex and reactive contaminants
unresolved.abstract: Non-sewered sanitation systems (NSSSs) are gaining global attention as decentralized solutions, yet the transformation of microplastics (MPs) within these systems remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate MP characteristics in the influent and effluent of two NSSSs using laser direct infrared spectroscopy, Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR MS), and liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). Both systems substantially reduce MP abundance (retention: 53.7–77.1%) but also alter MP characteristics. MPs exhibit fragmentation, reduced particle size, increased morphological irregularity, and surface oxidation, evidenced by decreased spectral matching scores and emerging oxygen-containing functional groups. FT-ICR MS reveals molecular-level oxidation enrichment, and over 260 candidate plastic additives are identified. LC-MS/MS confirms elevated phthalate ester concentrations, including DBP and DEHP. Statistical analyses link MP fragmentation, oxidation, and additive release as coupled processes. These findings suggest that NSSSs reshape MPs into more chemically reactive forms, highlighting the need to evaluate transformation-associated risks beyond retention efficiency. Microplastics are known to be present within non-sewered sanitation systems, but how treatment processes alter their physicochemical properties is not well underst

unresolved.title: Periodontal pathogen Tannerella forsythia promotes liver fibrosis via ICAM-1⁺ neutrophil–dependent hepatic stellate cell activation
unresolved.abstract: Periodontitis is a key driver in the development and progression of liver fibrosis. Nevertheless, how specific periodontal pathogens contribute to liver fibrosis remains elusive. Here, we identify Tannerella forsythia as the crucial mediator in the link between periodontitis and liver fibrosis, which can translocate to the gut and aggravate liver fibrosis. Mechanistically, Tannerella forsythia promotes the infiltration of ICAM-1+ neutrophils and inflammatory response in the liver via disrupting intestinal barrier integrity. ICAM-1+ neutrophils secrete TNF-α, which activates the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway in hepatic stellate cells, triggering collagen deposition and fibrogenesis. Conditional knockout of ICAM-1 in neutrophils or global deletion of TNF-α significantly attenuates inflammatory response and liver fibrosis caused by Tannerella forsythia. Taken together, this study identifies an oral-gut-liver axis driven by Tannerella forsythia and provides a prospective therapeutic target for periodontitis-related liver fibrosis. Peridontitis has been linked in the development and progression of liver fibrosis. Here the authors suggest that Tannerella forsythia is linked to the promotion of liver fibrosis by ICAM-1+ neutrophils activating hepatic stellate cells.

unresolved.title: Pipeline infrastructure for hydrogen transport in the United States
unresolved.abstract: Pipeline infrastructure is crucial for regional hydrogen transport. However, existing pipeline models have remarkably underestimated the construction-related material and labor costs compared to U.S. historical data. To cope with this problem and establish sustainable infrastructure, we develop integrated performance, economic and life cycle emissions models to comparatively evaluate dedicated pipelines and repurposed natural gas pipelines for hydrogen transport across the country. We find that the levelized cost of hydrogen transport via dedicated pipelines varies with numerous factors, such as location, capacity, and distance; there are similar variabilities in the cost of hydrogen transport via repurposed natural gas pipelines; and although leveraging existing natural gas pipelines can substantially reduce upfront capital expenditures, it may involve tradeoffs in cost and life cycle emissions. Here, we show that the integrated pipeline models and multi-criteria analysis can better guide engineering design, planning, and investment decisions on building nationwide hydrogen transport networks. This study compares new and repurposed gas pipelines for nationwide hydrogen transport, showing how costs and life-cycle emissions vary across options and highlighting trade-offs for infrastructure planning and investment.

unresolved.title: Precise polymerization of phenolic pollutants by a nanoconfined reactor with Fe-Mo dual-site
unresolved.abstract: The conversion of aquatic pollutants into polymers presents a significant opportunity for wastewater resource recovery. However, the precise synthesis of polymers with controlled molecular weight and narrow dispersity remains challenging. Herein, we design a spatially decoupled Fe-Mo dual-site catalyst (FeMo-NC), which synergistically regulates phenolic pollutant transformation through enhanced peroxymonosulfate activation and proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET), thereby reducing the C-H bond dissociation energy barrier by 18.3% and redirecting phenolic pollutant removal toward controlled oligomerization. By tuning the pore size of the carbon framework, we confine polymer growth, yielding polymers with molecular weights of 418–1142 g·mol−1 and narrow dispersity (PDI < 1.2). Compared to conventional Fe₃O₄/PMS systems, PMS consumption decreases by 96.7% and carbon emissions are significantly reduced. An integrated FeMo-NC/ceramic membrane (FeMo-NC/CM) system achieves 100% phenol (PhOH) removal over continuous operation exceeding 144 h. This work highlights confinement engineering as a strategy for selective organic polymerization and wastewater resource recovery. This work demonstrates a Fe-Mo dual-site catalyst that redirects phenolic pollutant transformation toward controlled oligomerization. The resulting membrane system achieves near-complete pollutant removal over 144 h

unresolved.title: Recognition and mechanism of M. tuberculosis cell wall galactan transport
unresolved.abstract: Mycobacterial-derived lipid-linked galactan (LLG) is an essential component of the Mycobacterial tuberculosis (Mtb) cell wall core arabinogalactan (AG), a well-established virulence factor and target of anti-tubercular drugs. Cross-membrane translocation of LLG is energetically unfavorable and is therefore catalyzed by WzmWzt, a prominent member of the polysaccharide ABC transporter sub-family. Here we present cryo-EM structures of WzmWztMtb to uncover critical steps of Mtb LLG translocation. Notably, densities suggestive of the mycobacterial-derived LLG substrates were observed in the structure of WzmWztMtb, indicating that the substrate may bind through two Wzm and two Wzt subunits. This proposed LLG binding is fulfilled by a fully upward extension of the Wzt gate helix, which serves as a critical step to prime Wzt for dimerization. The ATP-bound structure revealed a remarkable downward movement of the gate helix, together with the Wzt dimerization. The third, DDM/ATP-bound structure captured WztWzmMtb in an intermediate state with two DDM molecules in the Wzm central cavity. Using two conditional mycobacterial mutants for functional analyses, we have identified residues on the Wzm N-terminal interface helix (IFN) and on the Wzt helical domain are essential for LLG recognition and translocation in vivo. These data provide a clear structural basis for the development of Mtb ce

unresolved.title: Resistance indicators in sewage microbiota mirror clinical antibiotic use with temporal lag linked to host
unresolved.abstract: Wastewater-based surveillance (WBS) offers a promising window into community pathogens but extending it to antibiotic resistance (AR) is complicated by ecological and physical processes within sewer systems. The epidemiological meaning of antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) abundances in sewage remains unclear because signals reflect both human-derived inputs and in-sewer microbial dynamics. Using a unique 5-year dataset of outpatient antibiotic prescriptions and a yearlong, twice-weekly metagenomic survey of a single wastewater treatment plant, we differentiate associations between sewage-borne antibiotic-resistant bacteria and community antibiotic use. We find that ARGs linked to Enterobacteriaceae track closely with antibiotic usage, while those associated with ecologically-distinct Pseudomonadaceae show lagged correlations of 1–3 months. Nested statistical modeling further links Pseudomonas MAG dynamics with lagged sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim use after accounting for sewage characteristics and seasonality. Our results demonstrate that WBS can capture local patterns of epidemiologically relevant AR when microbial ecological factors shaping sewage signals are considered. Profiles of antibiotic resistance genes in wastewater still often lack epidemiological context. unresolved.title: Reversible dissociation of a sterically distorted dimer of a phosphagermylenylidene
unresolved.abstract: Accessing heavier analogues of isonitriles remains challenging because inefficient π overlap leads to weak and highly polarized π bonds that strongly favor dimerization or oligomerization. Herein, we report the experimentally observed dimer–monomer equilibrium of a phosphagermylenylidene in solution. Steric protection by a hydrindacenyl ligand renders the dimer highly sterically distorted and only weakly thermodynamically stabilized, enabling reversible dissociation to the monomer. The equilibrium has been studied by variable-temperature nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy in benzene-d6 solution, affording a modest driving force for dimerization (ΔHΘ = 16.26( ± 0.83) kcal mol−1 and ΔSΘ = 3.98( ± 0.26) × 10−2 kcal mol−1 K−1) through van’t Hoff analysis. The transient monomer can be trapped by the weak Lewis base tetrahydrofuran without substantial perturbation of the intrinsic P=Ge bonding. Both the dimer and the weakly coordinated monomer function as phosphagermylenylidene synthons, enabling C ≡ C and Si–H bond activation. These findings demonstrate that weak coordination combined with steric control provides a general strategy for accessing reactive heavier isonitrile analogues while preserving their intrinsic reactivity. unresolved.title: Single-cell atlas of fetal immunity across lung, spleen, and umbilical cord blood in nonhuman primates
unresolved.abstract: The fetal immune system develops within a tightly regulated environment that balances immune tolerance with readiness for postnatal antigen exposure. However, limited fetal tissue access constrains understanding of immune ontogeny across compartments. Here we present a multi-tissue single-cell transcriptional atlas of the late-gestation (GD130-135) rhesus macaque fetal immune system, profiling leukocytes from lung, spleen, and umbilical cord blood (UCBMC) spanning myeloid, lymphoid, innate lymphoid, and hematopoietic stem cell lineages. Fetal lung is enriched in myeloid cells and ILC2s and shows a proinflammatory bias. Spleen is dominated by T and B cells, with B cells showing enhanced signatures of V(D)J recombination and isotype switching and CD4 T cells showing increased activation and Treg frequency. UCBMC is predominantly composed of T cells with a regulatory transcriptional landscape. Spectral flow cytometry and functional assays corroborate these tissue-specific differences revealing elevated secretion of inflammatory mediators in fetal lung at rest, while spleen and UCBMC show greater inducible responses following stimulation. Together, these data provide a comprehensive cross-tissue atlas of late-gestation primate fetal immunity, revealing tissue-specific immune specialization, functional capacity, and intercellular communication networks that shape immune readiness pr

unresolved.title: Spinons, solitons and random-singlet-like behaviours in the spin-chain compound copper benzoate
unresolved.abstract: The S = 1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnetic chain is a paradigmatic quantum system hosting exotic excitations. Using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) on copper benzoate, we characterise three distinct types of excitations by tuning the magnetic field at ultra-low temperatures. At 0.2 T, a nearly constant spin-lattice relaxation rate (1/T1) and a divergence-like spin-spin relaxation rate (1/T2G) upon cooling provide experimental evidence for spinon excitations. Below 0.4 K, an additional relaxation channel, characterised by 1/T1 ∝ T with spectral weight growing as $$-\ln (T/{T}_{0})$$ and a divergence of the NMR Knight shift (Kn), reveals random-singlet-like behaviours. Above 1 T, a field-induced spin gap Δ ∝ H2/3 signifies the onset of soliton excitations. This work offers NMR identification of spinons, solitons, and the low-energy behaviours of a random-singlet-like state in copper benzoate, and establishes this material as a unique platform for studying the interplay of quantum integrability and disorder. A detailed low-temperature NMR study on copper benzoate reveals spinon excitations, low-temperature random-singlet-like behaviours and field-induced solitons, highlighting the interplay between crystal structure and weak disorder in a spin-chain system.

unresolved.title: The conformation-selective PI3Kδ inhibitor roginolisib in patients with advanced or metastatic cancer, including metastatic uveal melanoma: first-in-human clinical trial
unresolved.abstract: Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase delta (PI3Kδ) promotes tumour cell growth directly or indirectly by activating immune-suppressive cells. In contrast to previous PI3Kδ inhibitors, roginolisib is a selective, non-ATP competitive inhibitor, which locks PI3Kδ into an inactive state and causes an allosteric modulation. In a First-in-Human dose study, continuous daily dosing of roginolisib was investigated in patients with solid and haematologic malignancies. In Part A, 24 patients received escalating doses of roginolisib. In Part B, 20 mostly pre-treated metastatic uveal melanoma (mUM) patients received a dose associated with continuous PI3Kδ inhibition of >90%. The primary endpoint was safety, and secondary endpoints included pharmacokinetic (PK) and pharmacodynamic (PD) profile, clinical anti-tumour responses assessments. Exploratory endpoints included immunophenotyping, proteomics, genomics. No Dose Limiting Toxicity or drug related toxicities requiring dose modifications were observed ( ≥ Grade 3 toxicities: 3/44; 6.8%). In mUM, median Overall Survival (mOS) was 20.8 months (data-cut off December 2023) and 18.4 months (data-cut-off February 2026). mOS in mUM patients with Stable Disease at Week 16 ( = Cycle 5) was 28.5 months, while patients who progressed at Week 16 had a median OS of 12.3 months. unresolved.title: Topological diversity and scintillating dynamics of dipolar surface twists in a van der Waals magnet
unresolved.abstract: Realizing diverse configurations and dynamics of skyrmionic solitons offers additional topological and dynamical degrees of freedom for energy-efficient, topology-based spintronic devices. Extending these solitons into three dimensions further amplifies their potential, enabling the selective exploitation of surface- or bulk-topological characteristics, a regime that remains largely unexplored. Here, we report high-density dipolar-interaction-stabilized surface twists atop bulk stripe domains under zero magnetic field, through a systematic investigation of three-dimensional domain architectures in the room-temperature van der Waals ferromagnet Fe3GaTe2. Unlike conventional skyrmions with integer topological charges, these surface twists carry fractional charges and assemble into diverse composite configurations under field swapping, including aggregates of up to 13 surface twists and ring-like structures. Current-driven experiments uncover two distinct dynamic modes: scintillation, marked by the nucleation, annihilation, and helicity switching of surface twists, and ordered motion of bulk skyrmion strings. These behaviors arise from the interplay between spin-transfer torque and local pinning, establishing surface twists as tunable surface-localized topological states whose dynamics are decoupled from their bulk counterparts, thereby enabling versatile hybrid spintronic functio

unresolved.title: Outside Back Cover: Synthesis of Aminocyclopropanes by Redox‐Neutral Aminoalkylation
unresolved.abstract: In the Communication e8092854, Nuno Maulide and co-workers present a redox-neutral hydroaminoalkylation enabling access to aminocyclopropanes. This method utilizes a bench-stable hemiaminal and showcases a solvolysis-only activation, thus allowing broad substrate tolerance and orthogonality to traditional methods. A one-pot variant and pharmacological studies to demonstrate the power of aminocyclopropanes as bioisosteres for gem-alpha-dimethylamines further exemplify the utility of this work.

A universal twist-slide coupling mechanism governs deformations of DNA, RNA, and RNA-DNA hybrid duplexes
unresolved.abstract: Nucleic acid duplexes, including DNA, RNA, and RNA–DNA hybrid (RDH), undergo structural deformations that are essential for genome replication, transcription, and RNA-mediated regulation. However, quantitative measurements and mechanistic understanding of these deformations remain limited. Here, we probe nucleic acid deformations by measuring helical twist changes using single-molecule magnetic tweezers, where minute twist variations ( ~ 0.01° per base pair) accumulate over kilobase-length duplexes and become experimentally detectable. Unexpectedly, we find that RDHs do not behave as a simple intermediate between DNA and RNA. Instead, RDHs exhibit markedly attenuated twist responses to salt and temperature, together with nearly vanishing twist–stretch coupling. Despite these distinct mechanical behaviors, all-atom molecular dynamics simulations reveal a common deformation pathway shared by all three duplex types: external perturbations first modulate base-pair slide, which is subsequently transduced into twist changes through a universal twist–slide coupling. Building on this mechanism, we derive approximate theoretical predictions that quantitatively reproduce the salt- and temperature-dependent twist responses of RDH. We further show that protein-induced RDH deformations also occur predominantly along the twist–slide coupling pathway. Together, our results establish twist–sli

unresolved.title: ACAT1/SOAT1 governs mitochondrial dynamics and thermogenesis via the mTOR-MFN2-USP2 axis in brown adipocytes
unresolved.abstract: Mitochondrial dynamics are crucial for brown adipose tissue (BAT) thermogenesis and systemic energy homeostasis; yet, the cholesterol-sensing pathways regulating these processes remain poorly defined. Here we report that ACAT1, an endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-resident cholesterol esterase, acts as a critical rheostat of thermogenesis by governing mitochondrial dynamics in BAT. Mice with brown adipocyte-specific Acat1 deletion exhibit cold intolerance and exacerbated Western diet-induced obesity. Mechanistically, ACAT1 inhibition triggers intracellular cholesterol accu7mulation that activates mTOR-mediated phosphorylation of the mitochondrial fusion protein MFN2 at Serine 200. This modification recruits the deubiquitinase USP2, stabilizing MFN2 by inhibiting its proteasomal degradation and driving pathological mitochondrial fusion and ER-mitochondria contacts. Hence, our findings establish the ACAT1-mTOR-MFN2-USP2 axis as a fundamental mechanism coordinating cholesterol metabolism with mitochondrial dynamics, thermogenesis, and systemic energy balance, revealing its critical pathophysiological significance in obesity. Cholesterol levels must be precisely controlled in cells. Here, the authors identify the mTOR-MFN2-USP2 axis linking ACAT1-mediated cholesterol metabolism to mitochondrial homeostasis, critical for brown-fat thermogenesis and whole-body metabolism.

unresolved.title: Community-centric modeling of citation dynamics explains collective citation patterns across different knowledge systems
unresolved.abstract: Human knowledge systems, including science, law, and invention, are built on publications and the citations that link them. Statistical analysis of scientific citations has revealed patterns that illuminate the mechanisms driving knowledge production, recognition, and formalization. Yet most quantitative findings remain confined to science, leaving open the question of whether these dynamics are common features of how knowledge evolves. Here we show, using a corpus of U.S. case law alongside scientific and patent citations, that law, science, and patents share similar statistical citation dynamics. We propose a holistic model capturing three core mechanisms that drive collective dynamics, replicate observed citation patterns including previously unexplained phenomena like delayed recognition, and better predict future impact. Our findings suggest that common mechanisms govern large-scale patterns across diverse knowledge systems, offering generalizable perspectives on discovery and innovation. Science, law, and technology accumulate knowledge as people build on prior ideas through citations. Here, the authors show that shared citation patterns across these systems arise from collective exploration of a knowledge space.

unresolved.title: Earlier green-up exacerbates northern vegetation sensitivity to flash drought
unresolved.abstract: Flash drought–induced relative reduction in vegetation activity and canopy functioning, referred to as vegetation sensitivity, is a crucial measure of drought impacts. While climatic factors influencing vegetation sensitivity are well recognized, the role of phenological shifts remains poorly understood. Using multiple satellite-derived vegetation proxies (NDVI, LAI, SIF, and VOD) during 2001–2021, we show that earlier green-up dates (GUD) exacerbate vegetation sensitivity to flash droughts across 61.2–84.1% of the Northern Hemisphere (>23.5°N). Earlier GUDs enhance pre-drought vegetation growth, especially during the early growing season. Such amplified vegetation growth exacerbates sensitivity by accelerating soil moisture depletion and respiration cost, outweighing the benefit of increased subsequent net carbon assimilation. The contribution of GUD to vegetation sensitivity is comparable to that of major climatic factors. Ignoring phenological changes may lead to underestimation of long-term trends in vegetation sensitivity. These findings underscore the necessity of incorporating the interactions between phenology and flash droughts into projections of ecosystem resistance and resilience. Flash droughts can rapidly reduce vegetation growth, but the role of spring phenology is unclear. The authors show that earlier green-up increases vegetation sensitivity to flash drought a
topics: Plant Water Relations and Carbon Dynamics

unresolved.title: Estimating the completeness of large-scale single-cell sequencing projects
unresolved.abstract: During embryonic development, cells undergo differentiation into highly specialized cell types. Capitalizing on single-cell RNA sequencing, many initiatives and substantial resources are cataloguing these differentiated cell types by their transcriptomic profiles. Despite the extensive efforts to profile various organs and their cellular compositions, we lack metrics to assess the completeness of the sequencing projects. In this cellular biodiversity analysis, we leverage the increasingly available single-cell data together with statistical methods, originally developed for assessing the species richness of ecological communities, to estimate dataset completeness based on current data from single-cell profiling technologies. Deriving from such cellular richness estimates, we establish a practical statistical framework that enables reliable assessment of the completeness of any large-scale single-cell profiling project, after which additional sequencing efforts do not anymore reveal new cellular clusters. Such estimates can serve as stoppage-points for the ongoing sequencing projects, hence guiding a more cost-efficient completion of the profiling of various human tissues. Single-cell RNA sequencing is being widely used to catalogue differentiated cell types across tissues, but methods to evaluate how completely these cellular populations have been sampled remain limited. unresolved.title: Ethnicity, genomic ancestry, and HBV genotype in off-treatment outcomes following nucleos(t)ide analogue cessation: a prospective multicentre trial (COIN-B)
unresolved.abstract: Nucleos(t)ide analogue (NUC) cessation can induce functional cure, but outcomes vary. Ethnicity has been suggested as a determinant, but definitions are subjective and inconsistent. In this prospective, multicentre trial (NCT04779970, EudraCT 2021-001003-32), 91 long-term NUC-treated, start-of-treatment HBeAg-negative patients without advanced fibrosis discontinued treatment; 84 completed the 72-week protocol. In the prespecified analysis, off-treatment viral control at week 72 (primary endpoint) did not differ between Caucasians (n = 41) and non-Caucasians (n = 43) (41.5% vs 30.2%, p = 0.28). In exploratory analyses, HBsAg loss (7.1%, secondary endpoint) occurred exclusively in European or North African/Middle Eastern genomic ancestries, and ≥1 log IU/mL HBsAg decline was less frequent in Asian or Sub-Saharan African ancestries (p = 0.01). Lower end-of-treatment HBsAg independently predicted viral control, HBsAg loss and decline. Adjusted for end-of-treatment HBsAg, genotypes C and D achieved less viral control and required more retreatment than genotype A. Here, we show that genomic ancestry and HBV genotype capture clinically relevant heterogeneity, calling for more granular characterization of eligible populations. unresolved.title: Immune genetic associations of antibody Fc-profiles across twins
unresolved.abstract: Antibodies are bifunctional molecules that play a critical role in immune defense, both through their ability to recognize a near infinite number of targets via gene rearrangement and somatic hypermutation in their antigen-binding (Fab) region, and by directing the functional activity of the immune system via subclass/isotype switching and post-translational modifications of the fragment crystallizable (Fc) region. While genetic biases in Fab evolution have been demonstrated, less is known about the genetic regulation of Fc-biology. Thus, we comprehensively profiled 227 pathogen-specific antibody Fc-profiles to 20 antigens from 16 viral and bacterial pathogens and 2 allergens across a cohort of 510 monozygotic and dizygotic female twins. The majority of subclass, isotype, Fc-receptor binding, and Fc-effector functions show a degree of heritability. GWAS of the top 45 heritable phenotypes identified five genomic regions that are significantly associated with humoral traits and account for up to 33% of variance. Co-expression analysis in transcriptomic data indicated involvement of cytokine signaling, T cell help, and antigen presentation by myeloid cells as key potential regulators of Fc-biology. Collectively, these data highlight potential genetic mechanisms that govern Fc-biology. Fc-biology function may differ because of genetic heterogeneity. Here the authors profile antibod

unresolved.title: Modulate adsorption via Co2+-O-Coδ+ asymmetric pairs toward efficient upcycling of plastic waste to commodity chemicals
unresolved.abstract: The conversion of polyethylene terephthalate waste into valuable bulk chemicals through electrochemical upcycling represents a viable strategy for waste valorization. The direct involvement of hydroxyl species is crucial for C-C bond cleavage during ethylene glycol oxidation in polyethylene terephthalate hydrolysate, thereby enhancing catalytic efficiency. However, excessive or competitive hydroxyl adsorption often suppresses ethylene glycol adsorption and activation, impeding the formation of key intermediates toward formic acid. Here we show a crystal boundary engineering strategy to construct an asymmetric Co2+-O-Coδ+ bridged electrocatalyst within cobalt oxides. This design integrates two catalytic sites: Co2+ sites preferentially facilitate hydroxyl adsorption, while Coδ+ sites exhibit enhanced affinity for ethylene glycol, thereby reducing the energy barrier for formic acid formation. Consequently, the Asy-Co2+-O-Coδ+ exhibits a high Faradaic efficiency of 96.12% and selectivity of 93.75%. It delivers an industrial-level current density of 1000 mA cm−2 under membrane electrode assembly conditions, with competitive stability over multiple polyethylene terephthalate hydrolysate electrolysis cycles. This study provides valuable insights for the design of advanced catalysts in the upcycling of polyethylene terephthalate waste. Electrochemical oxidation of ethylene glycol offe

unresolved.title: Olaparib plus tremelimumab in women with recurrent ovarian cancer and a germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation: a phase I/II study
unresolved.abstract: Response rates to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) in ovarian cancer are low. In preclinical studies, poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibition (PARPi) synergized with CTLA4 ICB to achieve long-term survival in Brca1-deficient ovarian cancer models. Here we evaluated the safety and efficacy of combined treatment with the PARPi olaparib and the CTLA4 ICB tremelimumab for recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer in a multi-site single-arm phase I/II study enrolling 50 women with germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations (NCT02571725). In phase I, no new toxicities were identified (n = 3). In the combined phase I and II safety cohort (n = 49), 57% of subjects experienced grade 3 or 4 non-hematologic toxicity, with tremelimumab discontinuation in 34.7%. The primary phase II endpoint, overall response rate was 32.7% (95% CI 19.5-45.8%), and disease control rate was 47.7% (95% CI 33.0-62.5%). Secondary outcomes were progression-free survival (PFS, 3.0 months, 95% CI 2.7-5.9), and overall survival (24.3 months, CI 14.9-30.4). In exploratory post-hoc biomarker analyses, low VSTM5 or IFIT1B expression was associated with treatment benefit and improved PFS (p < 0.001). Although the trial did not meet its prespecified efficacy endpoint, PFS > 12 months in 6 subjects among this heavily pre-treated cohort highlight the need for biomarkers to select regimens for patients with recurrent ovarian cancer. unresolved.title: SWI/SNF subunit SMARCD1 deficiency promotes clear cell renal cell carcinoma progression via mitochondrial reprogramming
unresolved.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) remains a lethal malignancy driven in part by SWI/SNF dysfunction, yet the mechanistic basis of this link is unclear. We identify SMARCD1, a core SWI/SNF subunit, as a tumor suppressor progressively silenced by DNMT3B-mediated promoter hypermethylation in ccRCC. SMARCD1 loss enables DDX3X binding to the MAFF promoter, leading to transcriptional upregulation of MAFF, which in turn promotes ubiquitin-mediated degradation of the mitochondrial fusion protein MFN1. The SMARCD1–MAFF–MFN1 axis disrupts mitochondrial fusion, reprograms metabolism toward oxidative phosphorylation, and enhances metastatic potential. Therapeutically, pharmacological restoration of MFN1 with the FDA-approved immunosuppressant leflunomide reverses mitochondrial dysfunction and suppresses tumor progression in multiple preclinical models. In patient-derived xenografts, leflunomide also potentiates tyrosine kinase inhibitor and immune checkpoint blockade efficacy. These findings establish a direct link between chromatin remodeling defects and mitochondrial dysregulation and highlight leflunomide repurposing as a clinically actionable strategy in SMARCD1-deficient ccRCC. The SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complex is associated with cancer.
